item.title: Nintendo's Bill Trinen Explains Why Ocarina Of Time Is The Perfect Entry Point Into The Zelda Universe

description.p: Gather round, Kokiri.If you're in a position where you've never actually played a Zelda game before, Nintendo's Bill Trinen just wants to let you know Ocarina of Time is the "perfect place" to start.Although this comment just happens to line up with the arrival of the Switch 2 remake, Nintendo's VP of Player & Product Experience really is convinced this is the best game to begin with, as it's a "foundational story", where the player is taught everything they need to know about the world and characters.Read the full article on nintendolife.com

item.title: Digital Foundry Delivers Its Tech Verdict On Stellar Blade's Switch 2 Port

description.p: "Better than expected".Stellar Blade also arrived on the Switch 2 this week, and it's been positively received so far. Here on Nintendo Life, we gave it a score of seven out of ten, and although there are some technical drawbacks, Eve's outing stands tall on the hybrid platform.The team at Digital Foundry has now delivered its tech review of the Unreal Engine 4 title, and while it's no "tour de force", it does translate to a "better than expected Switch 2 port", with what's described as an experience with "gentler compromises" than many more recent titles.Read the full article on nintendolife.com

item.title: Zelda Producer Eiji Aonuma Talks About The Benefits Of "Long-Term-Tenured Staff" At Nintendo

description.p: "It contributes to some of the sense of continuity".One morsel from Nintendo's latest Ask the Developer interview revealed how the team behind the Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake got the artist "who had created illustrations for the N64 version" to draw a new map for the Switch 2 release.It's not every day developers reviving older games can directly consult original team members, but this is just one of many examples at Nintendo. Zelda producer, Eiji Aonuma, has now elaborated on the benefits of Nintendo's "long-term tenured staff members", explaining how it provides "balance" and the "sense of continuity" when crafting projects like the remake.Read the full article on nintendolife.com

item.title: PSA: Want To Learn Link's Ocarina Tunes? Nintendo's Got The Sheet Music For All Of Them

description.p: Hylian how-to.Whether you have been playing Ocarina of Time on Switch 2, watching the trailers, or just been in the ether of its release, you almost certainly have an ocarina melody or two stuck in your head right now. For those who want to channel their earworm into a lesson, Nintendo has shared the sheet music for each of Link's in-game tunes, so you can stop whistling Zelda's Lullaby and learn to play it instead.Nintendo previously announced that it'd share music how-tos via the Zelda Notes app, so you could work out how to play the tunes on any real-world ocarinas you may have accumulated over the years. But look, all of them are also available on the game's Japanese website, so you don't need to worry about unlocking them in-game before you start learning!Read the full article on nintendolife.com

item.title: Are You A Tired Parent? The Witcher 3's New Accessibility Mode Was Built With You In Mind

description.p: For anyone busy adulting.CD Projekt Red's director of player experience, Karolina Niewęgłowska, has taken to the company's official forum to explain the approach behind a new accessibility preset for The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt - Remastered (thanks, Push Square).Dubbed 'Bard's Ballad', this option contains a number of individual accessibility toggles that you can tinker with to suit your own needs, or you can simply apply all of them at once as a blanket preset. So for example, this includes disabling item weight and durability along with the ability to disable herb icons on the mini-map.Read the full article on nintendolife.com
